skill.name: prisma-client-api
skill.description: Reference Prisma Client queries, filters, relations, transactions, raw SQL, lifecycle methods, and constructor options for current TypeScript database projects.
skill.summary: Build type-safe Prisma Client operations with focused API guidance and practical examples.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: All 151 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, TypeScript templates, relative imports, environment configuration, SQL examples, and documentation links. No command execution, path traversal, environment-file reading, reconnaissance, unauthorized network behavior, or prompt injection was found. One medium concern remains because examples log raw query parameters without redaction and may expose sensitive data.

remediation.issue: Raw query parameter logging can expose sensitive values.
remediation.suggestion: Add redaction guidance, omit e.params from production logs, and show development-only logging with an explicit environment guard.

content.value_statement: Prisma Client APIs can be difficult to navigate across queries, filters, relations, transactions, and configuration. This reference provides focused patterns and examples for common Prisma Client tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains PrismaClient construction with driver adapters, Accelerate, logging, transaction defaults, and singleton patterns.
Covers common model methods for reading, creating, updating, deleting, counting, aggregating, and grouping records.
Shows field selection, relation inclusion, omission, filtering, sorting, cursor pagination, and distinct results.
Documents relation queries, relation filters, nested writes, and relation counts.
Demonstrates sequential and interactive transactions with isolation, rollback, and transaction-client guidance.
Compares parameterized raw query APIs, dynamic SQL fragments, database-specific queries, and explicitly unsafe variants.
limitations: This reference does not inspect your schema, execute queries, manage migrations, or verify database results.
Generated-client import paths and model names require adaptation to your project structure.
The skill declares version 7.6.0; verify APIs against your installed Prisma packages.
Raw SQL and query logging examples still require application-specific security review.

use_cases.title: Implement backend data access
use_cases.description: Choose typed Prisma methods, filters, relations, and result shapes for an application feature.

use_cases.title: Design reliable transactions
use_cases.description: Select sequential or interactive transactions and define suitable timeouts, isolation, and rollback behavior.

use_cases.title: Review query security
use_cases.description: Check raw SQL parameterization, sensitive field selection, query logging, and destructive operations before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic query
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my User model requirements, explain a Prisma Client findMany query with filters, sorting, and a result limit.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs a first read query.

prompt_templates.title: Add relations and pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Prisma query that selects specific user fields, includes recent posts, and uses cursor pagination. Explain each option.
prompt_templates.scenario: An API endpoint needs bounded relational data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an account transaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose an interactive transaction for transferring account funds. Include validation, isolation guidance, rollback behavior, and limits on external work.
prompt_templates.scenario: A financial workflow needs atomic database changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an advanced data layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my Prisma Client setup and raw SQL approach for injection, connection handling, transaction boundaries, sensitive logging, and type safety.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs a comprehensive production assessment.

output_examples.input: Find active users, return only required fields, and paginate the results.
output: Recommended method: findMany with an active-status filter, descending creation order, and a bounded result size.
Field selection: return only identifiers, names, and email addresses required by the caller.
Pagination note: use a stable unique cursor for subsequent pages.

output_examples.input: Choose a transaction strategy for transferring funds between two accounts.
output_examples.output: Use an interactive transaction with validated account records, guarded balance changes, a strict timeout, and no external network work inside the transaction.

output_examples.input: Review a raw SQL search that includes user input.
output: Risk: unsafe raw SQL interpolation can permit injection.
Safer approach: use parameterized tagged templates and allowlist any dynamic identifiers.
Logging note: redact query parameters before sending events to application logs.

best_practices: Prefer generated Prisma types and parameterized query APIs for application data.
Select only required fields, bound result sizes, and use stable cursor pagination.
Keep transactions short and redact sensitive query parameters before logging.
anti_patterns: Do not interpolate untrusted input into unsafe raw SQL strings.
Do not log database parameters without redaction and production controls.
Do not run unfiltered bulk updates or deletes without explicit review.

faq.question: Does this skill execute database queries?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance and examples; your application and Prisma Client perform all database operations.

faq.question: Which Prisma version does it cover?
faq.answer: The skill declares version 7.6.0. Confirm APIs against the Prisma packages installed in your project.

faq.question: Can it help with raw SQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers parameterized raw queries, dynamic fragments, unsafe variants, and SQL injection prevention.

faq.question: Does it configure my database connection?
faq.answer: It explains constructor and adapter patterns, but you must supply and protect your connection settings.

faq.question: Can it create schemas or migrations?
faq.answer: No. The reference focuses on Prisma Client APIs, not schema design, generation, or migration workflows.

faq.question: How should I protect sensitive data?
faq.answer: Select only required fields, parameterize inputs, redact query logs, and review all destructive operations.
